name: Nahash
overview: Nahash is a female figure noted primarily as the mother of Abigail according to 2 Samuel 17:25. While there is some suggestion that she may be the wife of Jesse, David's father, this is not definitively established. There is no recorded tribal affiliation or additional notes about her in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Nahash means 'viper' or 'copper' in Hebrew, as indicated in 2 Samuel 17:25. This proper name does not appear to have been given by God but reflects a common Hebrew personal name of the time.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Nahash as the mother of Abigail, as stated in 2 Samuel 17:25. Beyond this maternal relationship, there is no explicit biblical record of other family ties, although there is an inferred connection to Jesse as her husband.
scriptureSignificance: Nahash's significance in the biblical narrative is primarily connected to her role as the mother of Abigail, who is mentioned in the context of David's story. Her mention, though brief, situates her within the lineage related to King David, highlighting the human connections behind the biblical figures. This underscores the providential preservation of David's family line and God's sovereign plan in history.
